subsystems.name: Individual robot units
subsystems.role: simple, comparatively cheap agents; capability comes from numbers, not from any one unit.

subsystems.name: Localisation and neighbour sensing
subsystems.role: each unit must know roughly where it is and who is nearby — usually without GPS.

subsystems.name: Communication network
subsystems.role: peer-to-peer message passing with no central hub, so losing one node does not stop the group.

subsystems.name: Collective control algorithms
subsystems.role: local rules that add up to useful group behaviour.

subsystems.name: Operator interface
subsystems.role: a human states intent once; the swarm works out the detail.

subsystems.name: Power and logistics
subsystems.role: keeping dozens to hundreds of units charged, stored and deployable.

buildSteps.title: Decompose the task into local rules
buildSteps.detail: The mission is rewritten so each robot only needs its own state and what it senses or hears from neighbours — no unit sees the whole picture.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of virtual agents are run in physics simulation to check that the intended group behaviour emerges and survives dropouts.

buildSteps.title: Design and build one unit
buildSteps.detail: A single robot is prototyped with the cheapest sensors and radio that will do the job, since unit cost sets how large a swarm is affordable.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and calibrate a batch
buildSteps.detail: Identical units are assembled and individually calibrated, because small sensor and motor differences between robots can break coordinated motion.

buildSteps.title: Build the test arena
buildSteps.detail: An indoor space with overhead camera tracking or ultra-wideband anchors gives ground-truth positions; wider outdoor sites are used later.

buildSteps.title: Run up the network and localisation
buildSteps.detail: Mesh radios are configured, ranging and clock sync tested, and message-passing checked as robot numbers grow.

buildSteps.title: Tune the collective behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Parameters are adjusted through hundreds of trials until the swarm forms shapes, spreads to search, or covers an area reliably despite failed units.

buildSteps.title: Trial with operators
buildSteps.detail: Swarms are put through realistic search, inspection or monitoring scenarios where a human issues only high-level commands.

buildSteps.title: Harden and certify
buildSteps.detail: Fail-safes, jamming and spoofing resilience, geofencing and airspace or workplace rules are added before routine deployment.

prerequisites.why: swarm behaviour only pays off when a unit costs little enough to field hundreds of them.
decentralised coordination depends on robots relaying messages to each other without infrastructure.
indoors, under canopy or in rubble, ultra-wideband and visual methods work but are less robust than satellite fixes.
emergent behaviour is hard to prove safe; simulation plus formal methods are needed before operators will trust it.
short battery life still limits missions unless robots can dock, swap packs or be retrieved on their own.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms of hundreds of small robots demonstrating self-assembly, shape formation and area coverage, plus shared remote testbeds
pathway.unlocks: proof that simple local rules scale to large, robust group behaviour.

pathway.milestone: outdoor field swarms of tens to a few hundred aerial and ground units under one operator, as shown in defence research programmes
pathway.unlocks: practical search-and-rescue and surveillance coverage over real terrain.

pathway.milestone: mixed swarms of drones, ground vehicles and boats sharing one task allocation
pathway.unlocks: persistent environmental monitoring and inspection of large infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: self-repairing swarms with certified safety and airspace integration
pathway.unlocks: routine civilian use in disaster response, agriculture and logistics.
